items.stem: What is Human Development ? Explain its indicators.
items.answer: Human development is about expanding the richness of human life rather than simply the richness of the economy in which human beings live. It is an approach focused on people and on their opportunities and choices. Its indicators are: (1) Life expectancy at birth — the number of years a newborn infant could expect to live if the prevailing patterns of age-specific mortality rates at the time of birth remained the same throughout the infant's life. (2) Mean years of schooling — the average number of years of education received by people aged 25 and older, converted from education attainment levels using the official duration of each level. (3) Expected years of schooling — the number of years of schooling a child of school entrance age can expect to receive if prevailing patterns of age-specific enrolment rates persist throughout the child's life. (4) Gross National Income (GNI) per capita — the aggregate income of an economy generated by its production and its ownership of factors of production, less the incomes paid for the use of factors of production owned by the rest of the world, converted to international dollars using purchasing power parity (PPP) rates and divided by mid-year population. (5) Non-income Human Development Index — the value of the HDI computed from the life expectancy and education indicators only. Thus human development measures people's well-being through health, education and income indicators.

items.stem:
What is meant by ‘Land degradation’. Which are the factors responsible for land degradation ?
or
Explain any four human activities which are mainly responsible for land degradation in India.
items.answer: Land degradation means the deterioration of the quality of land, which makes it unfit for any use because of various human activities. The factors responsible for it are: (1) Deforestation, which leaves the land bare so that natural forces act upon it and the quality of land diminishes. (2) Overgrazing by animals, which contributes significantly to degradation. (3) Mining — mines are abandoned once excavation is over, leaving the land full of heaps and pits, so that it becomes unfit for agriculture and other economic activities. (4) Over irrigation, which causes water logging and thereby increases salinity and alkalinity in the soil. (5) Grinding of limestone for the cement industry and of calcite and soapstone for the ceramic industry, which produces heavy amounts of dust that settles in the surrounding areas, spoiling the land and badly affecting crop cultivation. Hence land degradation in India is mainly the result of deforestation, overgrazing, mining, over irrigation and industrial dust.

items.stem:
How can the problems of land degradation be solved? Give any four measures.
or
What are the reasons for land degradation? Describe briefly any four measures to conserve land from degradation.
items.answer: Land degradation means the deterioration of the quality of land, which makes it unfit for any use because of various human activities. Measures to solve the problem are: (1) Afforestation — vegetation provides a protective cover to the land and does not allow rainwater to fall straight on it, thus helping to maintain soil fertility. (2) Shelter belts can be created on the margins of desert areas. (3) In semi-arid areas degradation can be curbed by cultivation techniques based on moisture conservation. (4) Industrial effluents and wastes are a major cause of degradation, so effective measures must be taken for their proper discharge and disposal. (5) Overgrazing of land by animals must be controlled. (6) Shifting sand dunes in desert areas should be stabilised by planting thorny bushes. Adopting these measures conserves land and checks further degradation.

items.stem: Imagine yourself as one of the heads of the states attending the International Earth Summit at Rio-de Janeiro, Brazil and suggest some methods for environment protection.
items.answer: Speaking as the head of India at the International Earth Summit at Rio-de Janeiro, Brazil, the following methods are suggested to combat environmental damage, poverty and disease: (1) The environment should be protected at all cost throughout the world through the mutual understanding of all countries — land, air and soil should be conserved and protected from pollution, and forests, wildlife and aquatic animals should be protected. (2) Poverty should be removed by the creation of new jobs; globalisation and liberalisation should be adopted by all countries, liberal financial help should be extended by the Super Powers to poor and needy countries, and the latest developed technology should be provided to all developing countries. (3) Diseases of every kind, especially the serious and harmful ones, should be faced with mutual medical help and the exchange of doctors, surgeons, experts, knowledge and medical equipment. To achieve our goal, sustainable economic development should be promoted in all countries without damaging the environment, and at present we should not compromise with the needs of future generations during the process of development.

items.stem: What do you mean by ‘land use pattern’ ? Name the factors that determine the use of land.
items.answer: Land use pattern means the utilisation of land for various purposes such as cultivation, grazing of animals, mining, and the construction of buildings, roads and railways. The factors that determine the use of land are: (1) Topography — steeply sloping land is not suitable for cultivation, marshy lands cannot be used unless they are properly drained, and rocky lands with soil cover are unfit for cultivation though they may provide grazing areas; it is mainly the well-drained fertile lowlands that are put to diverse economic uses. (2) Climate — India is a tropical country with a year-round growing season except in the mountains, which makes our land more valuable for high agricultural productivity and for the growth of natural vegetation, and accounts for the growing of a large variety of crops throughout the year. (3) Accessibility — lands accessible by roads and railways are more suitable for human habitation and economic activities. (4) Population density, technological capability, culture and traditions are other factors that determine the use of land.

items.stem: Explain the role of human in resource development.
items.answer: Human beings play a decisive role in the development of resources: (1) They should not use resources indiscriminately, because indiscriminate use has led to a global ecological crisis marked by global warming, ozone layer depletion, environmental pollution and land degradation. (2) Resources should not be allowed to accumulate in a few hands, since this divides society into two segments, the haves and the have-nots, or the rich and the poor. (3) Resource planning should be done for sustainable development, that is, development should take place without damaging the environment, and development in the present should not be compromised with the needs of future generations. (4) Conservation of resources should be given priority because they are vital for developmental activity. (5) Optimum utilisation of resources needs to be practised, since resources are available in fixed quantity and cannot be reproduced or renewed. Thus it is human beings who, through planning, conservation and judicious use, turn the physical environment into resources and decide how long those resources will last.
